children: Kavaljer Investmentbolagsfond gained 1.8% in August, compared with 1.9% for the Stockholm Stock Exchange (OMXSPI-GI) and 2.8% for the global equity market (Dow Jones World Index). The largest positive contributors during the month were Bure Equity, Danaher and Microsoft, while HBM Healthcare, Alphabet and Markel detracted the most from performance.
Strong earnings season and narrowing discounts to NAV

Like July, August was a strong month for equity markets. The second-quarter earnings season showed that the fund’s holdings are generally performing well. Among the fund’s serial acquirers, revenue increased by an average of 10%, while operating profit rose by just over 13%, exceeding expectations. Meanwhile, growing optimism in Swedish industry was clearly reflected in order intake at companies such as Latour.

Among the investment companies, Bure Equity stood out positively, with its discount to net asset value narrowing from 22% to 8%. By contrast, Prosus’ discount widened from 37% to 40% amid continued share-price weakness.
During the month, the fund reduced its holding in Bure Equity and fully divested its position in Idun Industrier, while increasing its holding in Alphabet. The equity exposure amounted to 99%.
In-depth review of the fund’s holdings

This month’s in-depth review covers, among other topics, Latour’s significantly improved order intake following its second-quarter report, Ratos’ ongoing divestment process for KVD, Siemens’ broad exposure to the expansion of AI infrastructure, and Ametek’s strong quarter, with accelerating order intake.
Read the full monthly report in the attached file.
